title: The critical strip
mathematical_role: Give an exact symbolic analytic frame for the critical strip, critical line, pole, trivial zeros, and the two standard zero symmetries without decorative nontrivial-zero placement.
learning_objective: Locate the Riemann hypothesis in the complex plane while separating exact symbolic structure from finite numerical zero data.
literal_semantics: The plate uses the coordinate s = σ + it with explicit Re(s) and Im(s) axes.
The lines Re(s)=0, Re(s)=1, and Re(s)=1/2 are explicitly labelled.
The pole at s=1 is separately identified.
The negative-even trivial zeros −2, −4, and −6 are shown on a separate exact real-axis context.
The symbolic symmetries ρ ↦ 1−ρ and ρ ↦ ρ̄ are explicitly stated.
No numerical nontrivial-zero coordinates are plotted.
nonliteral_semantics: The finite set of displayed trivial zeros is illustrative of the negative-even family rather than exhaustive.
Symmetry arrows are explanatory annotations rather than trajectories in the complex plane.
The plate does not encode zero multiplicities.

notes: The successor intentionally avoids numerical nontrivial-zero data, so no finite zero dataset is introduced by this operation.

renderer.version_or_environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic SVG renderer v1
reproducibility_notes: No randomness or external service is used.
Run the generator from any checkout; output paths and bytes are deterministic under the recorded Python-standard-library contract.

derivatives.role: exact symbolic vector master; web and print/review candidate

accessibility.alt_text: A complex-plane critical-strip frame labels real parts zero, one-half, and one; the pole at one, selected negative-even trivial zeros, and functional and conjugation symmetries are shown, with no numerical nontrivial zeros plotted.
accessibility.long_description: The main panel shades the strip from real part zero to one and marks the critical line at one-half. Re(s) and Im(s) axes are explicit, and the pole at s=1 is marked on the real axis. Text identifies functional-equation and conjugation symmetries. A separate lower real-axis panel marks −6, −4, and −2 as trivial zeros. The plate explicitly says no finite nontrivial-zero dataset is plotted and states RH only as the assertion that all nontrivial zeros have real part one-half.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Exact symbolic exposition of the analytic geography in which the Riemann hypothesis is stated.
not_claimed: Verification of any numerical nontrivial zero

supersession_reason: The successor replaces decorative generic points with exact labelled analytic structure and explicitly declines to plot unbound nontrivial-zero coordinates.
